To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have identified a unique proteomic profile of lamellar bodies from amniotic-fluid, which are likely derived from fetal lung, and that the profile suggests a role for these secretions in innate host defense.
the amniotic LB proteome is distinct from that of the epidermis, but similar to the rat lung proteome.
we have identified 122 unique protein in LBs isolated from term amniotic fluid, and that the preponderence of these proteins is associated with host defense.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of proteins in LBs secreted into the AF and the role of these proteins in the biogenesis and functions of LBs in the AF.
the identification and characterization of proteins that are secreted by the fetal lung and enter the amniotic cavity.
the identification and characterization of the proteins that are secreted from the fetal lung and enter the amniotic cavity during the final stages of fetal development.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proteins in the amniotic LB are not the same as those in the skin LB, and the proteins in the lung LBs are similar to the proteins in the fetal amniotic LBs.
amniotic LBs are derived predominantly from lung secretions, and they play an important role as innate immune defense of the fetus.
amniotic fluids are not simply the waste products of the fetus.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proteins identified in the LBs isolated from the amniocentesis samples are consistent with those that are known to be expressed in lung and are consistent with a role in innate host defence.

we have demonstrated for the first time that amniotic fluids contain lamellar bodies (Lamellar bodies are secretory organelles in epithelial cells that contain phospholipids, proteins, and enzymes) and that the proteins in the lamellar bodies are different from those in other epithelial cells.
the proteins found in the LBs of amniotic fluids are similar in composition to those found in LBs from lung secretions, suggesting that amniotic LBs are derived in large measure from the lung.
The main takeaway from our work is that
LBs isolated from the amniocentesis specimens of term pregnancies have a distinct proteome compared with LBs isolated from human epidermis.
amniotic LBs are not just a marker of fetal lung maturity but are a unique secreted product of the lung that is likely to have important functions in fetal health.
the amniotic LBs are different from the skin LBs and that these amniotic LB proteins may play a role in innate immune function in the fetus.
